gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-armata: Bold and tube-bright, Tilt Neon sets one constant stroke against a wide, gappy lowercase. Armata sans-serif follows with spacious gaps between its characters, so the loud heading never crowds the text.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-athiti: Athiti has a sans build with a high mean line and an s you can see through, friendly and contemporary. Under Tilt Neon's tube-like display lettering, the text feels easygoing.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-atkinson-hyperlegibl: Tilt Neon hits hard: tube-like strokes, big lowercase, short ascenders. Atkinson Hyperlegible keeps its wide-set s terminals and clipped capitals, so a long stretch of text feels approachable and steady, never fussy.

Tilt Neon's splayed c terminal and tube-like strokes give it away, with no thick and thin in any letter. Yet Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono does the quieter work, its open counters letting plain sans text breathe in the white space.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-biryani: Tilt Neon brings a splayed c terminal and a tube-like, constant-width stroke to the top of the page. Biryani, a plain sans, keeps its e eyes clear below.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-blinker: Commanding in its tube-like display strokes, Tilt Neon sits over Blinker, a plain sans with open apertures and a lowercase that fills most of its height. Shrink the heading and its punch fades.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-carrois-gothic: Carrois Gothic reads modern and professional, with a high-set x-height and a generous opening in c. Tilt Neon is the louder one, its tube-like stroke holding thickness around every curve, while Carrois Gothic handles the text.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Loud tubes up top, quiet curves below. And Carrois Gothic SC keeps a clear opening at the end of every curve, so a longer passage reads smoothly and approachably.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-chivo: Big, bold tube lettering up top. Chivo takes over where Tilt Neon's gauge-steady strokes shout, packing its lowercase tight toward the caps with visible daylight through every curve.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-chocolate-classical-: Tilt Neon has a splayed c terminal and no calligraphic thinning, while Chocolate Classical Sans, a plain sans, keeps a broad-nibbed stroke. Make the heading small and its boldness drains away.
